title: Made a dark castle builder with AI tools. 8 of my last 37 players quit within a minute. What am I missing?
author: Curious_Ad5417
selftext:
Grauwacht is a dark medieval castle builder with beast hunting. You inherit a ruin, rebuild it, train hunters and send them after 60 beasts that bite back. There’s also a small card game at the inn. It’s free in the browser on phone or desktop, the Android app is in closed testing, and it runs in five languages.

Since this sub is about how things get made: the code is written with Claude Code. I describe what I want, read what comes back, playtest, complain, repeat. It also wrote automated playtests that click every button on phone and desktop sizes, which found bugs I would never have found myself (my favourite: map points you simply couldn’t click with a mouse). The painted scenes and item art come from ChatGPT image generation, held together by a fixed style guide so it doesn’t look like ten different games. The town map and the people walking around it are rendered in Blender, and some of the beasts started as Meshy models before getting their own rigs. Translations are AI drafted too, so if you speak Spanish, French or Portuguese, feel free to laugh at me.

Now the humbling part. I added anonymous counters and the last 7 days say, 37 new players, 8 gone within the first minute, 18 within ten minutes, and 11 never placed a single building. In a building game. So almost a third of my players decided the best part of a building game is not building. Fair, but I’d love to know why.

If you have 5 minutes, play from the prologue to your first building and tell me where you got bored, lost or annoyed. Be blunt, I can take it (probably). If you’re more into cards, the card game also runs on its own: [https://grauwacht.com/pirsch?von=reddit-aig](https://grauwacht.com/pirsch?von=reddit-aig)

[https://grauwacht.com/start?von=reddit-aig](https://grauwacht.com/start?von=reddit-aig)

No account needed to try it.

comments.author: 3tt07kjt
comments.body: I don’t know what the goal of the game is or what the stakes are (how I could fail or lose).

replies.author: Curious_Ad5417
replies.body: That’s a really useful point, thank you. The goal is to rebuild a ruined keep from level 1 to 30, and each level open the next chapter of the story. Along the way you hunt 60 beasts, and a hunt can go wrong if you pick something your hunters can’t handle yet. But you’re right that the opening doesn’t say any of that clearly. What would have helped you more, a clear goal on the first screen or a sense of danger early on?

replies.author: 3tt07kjt
replies.body: Which would have helped me more? I honestly don’t know. It is really your job to figure that part out. Playtesters can tell you where the problem is, but it’s up to you to figure out what the solution is.

replies.author: Curious_Ad5417
replies.body: Fair point, that one’s on me. You showed me where it hurts, which was the part I couldnt see myself. Thanks for taking the time.

comments.author: Upstairs_Weird_760
comments.body: Probably cause the card game aspect.

replies.author: Curious_Ad5417
replies.body: Could be, but the card game is just a little side thing for in between. The cards come from your hunts, so it mostly gives the hunting a bit more meaning. The main game is rebuilding the keep and sending hunters after beasts. Was it the mention of cards that put you off, or something in the first minute itself?

comments.author: HECRETSECRET
comments.body:
It looks like a mobile phone game and feels like a genric ai mobile game with no heart or story/ involvement. 

The card game looks boring, the story introduction is boring, and the castle builder the typical thing that would be okay a decade ago but has done a million times and has no interest. 

It looks like you are some sort of bot, but everything about this is just blah and boring.

replies.author: Curious_Ad5417
replies.body: Ouch, but fair enough, and thanks for actually trying it. Not a bot, just a guy who should probably be asleep by now. The boring story intro lines up with my numbers, that’s exactly where most people drop off so that one goes straight on the list. was there anything at all that felt like it had a bit of heart, or was it blah from the first screen?

replies.author: ScurrHannes
replies.body:
tbh i only played for like 1 min and it was already enougth for me personaly.  
it feels and looks like a ai slop game that misses out on liveliness and kinda hits like an unorganised mess.

replies.author: Curious_Ad5417
replies.body: Fair, a minute is exactly the window I’m trying to fix, so this helps more than you’d think. Misses liveliness is a good way to put it, the start is mostly text and still pictures right now. Thanks for being honest.

replies.author: HECRETSECRET
replies.body:
Nothing feels any heart at all. There is too much indentifable dark ai stuff here. 

This is just flawed story telling and establishing what the stakes are but equally dark fantasy kingdom builder should not feel like im manning a time simulator behind a computer.

replies.author: Curious_Ad5417
replies.body: That “time simulator” line stings because it’s fair. The first minutes are mostly watching numbers go up. I already moved the first hunt to the very start today, but you’re right that there are no real stakes yet. If you opened a game like this, what would make you care in the first minute? A threat at the gate, a person you meet, something else?

comments.author: Seven-Prime
comments.body:
Gave it a quick shot. Quite a bit a of startup before I even play. It's not clear what I'm supposed to do. I clicked some buttons a progress bar moved across the screen.

Hope this helps.

replies.author: Curious_Ad5417
replies.body: It does help, thanks for giving it a shot. You re the third person saying roughly the same thing, so the start is clearly my problem. Out of curiosity, at which point would you have wanted to actually do something? Right after the first screen?

comments.author: SlightOfHand_
comments.body: Front loading it with an AI art slideshow and then requiring an email login seems like it will filter a lot of people

replies.author: Curious_Ad5417
replies.body: Yeah, thats the clearest summary anyone gave me today. You can actually play without an account, but the start makes it look like you cant, which is just as bad. Im cutting the intro down to one screen and dropping the account step before you play. Thanks!

comments.author: jpewaqs
comments.body:
I played a bit and to be blunt is a bit boring. You click a few buttons and all you get is a timer counting down. I'm guessing as soon as these reach zero you click a few more buttons for another timer to appear only this time for longer. 
There is a literally no reason to wait or return.

replies.author: Curious_Ad5417
replies.body: Fair, timer games aren’t for everyone, and thats okay. But youre right that my start shows the timers long before it shows anything worth waiting for. The hunting and the story are meant to be the reason to come back, and right now you have to dig to even find them. Im reworking the first minutes so you get to a fight before you ever have to wait. What would have made you curious enough to return?

replies.author: jpewaqs
replies.body:
Timer games can be fun, but they are all designed in a specific way that yours isn't. The first 10 to 20 levels are all very short time, meaning as you explore the game you're constantly returning to press the next button to upgrade. You essentially can spend the first thirty minutes or hour on it and consistently have something different to do.  Then once the core mechanics are developed and understood the timer starts to lengthen, and this is where the mechanics of purchasing speed/time boosts come in.  
  
In your game the first button was an almost instant upgrade and the second had a 1hour timer. There isn't anything which suggests what to do while you wait and i'm sorry but nobody is hanging round more than a minute when they realise they've to wait an hour.

replies.author: Curious_Ad5417
replies.body: Thanks, thats fair feedback. You played an older version, since then the first builds finish instantly and the first hunt plays as a short fight. Waiting is part of the genre later on, but you’re right that it shouldn’t hit before you’ve seen what’s worth waiting for.

comments.author: Visual_Psychology_9
comments.body: Tried it, lasted 2 minutes. It needs polishing in every aspect. Clicked on keep and automatically upgraded, got a reward, was told to upgrade something else, i did, got another reward, annoying kite in the middle of the screen, really blurry graphics, four screens of blah I didn't read at the start.

replies.author: Curious_Ad5417
replies.body: Thanks, thats a really concrete list. The four screens of intro are getting cut down to one, that’s already in the works after today. Two questions so I fix the right thing, what was the kite in the middle of the screen, something flying over the town? And were you on a phone or a big monitor when it looked blurry?

comments.author: inr222
comments.body:
I don't think it does anything interesting to attract attention. Also the art is clearly recognizable as AI art, which reads as low effort.
My first reaction is "this is slop and not worth my time".
Didn't get pass the first menu.

replies.author: Curious_Ad5417
replies.body: Thanks for being straight about it. If the first screen already says “not worth my time”, that screen has failed, whatever comes after. Thats useful to know.

comments.author: TheCentralPosition
comments.body: The description made me think of Darkest Dungeon, a game whose gameplay I don't love but whose art, VA, and premise kept me around for a while despite that. I skipped the tutorial, I prefer to learn as I go. Clicked into a card game and left pretty quickly. I am not a fan of card games, and nothing about the experience or presentation of it was unique or flavorful enough to pique my interest get past that initial turn-off.

replies.author: Curious_Ad5417
replies.body: Thats on me for putting the card game link in the post, it’s really just a small side thing at the inn. The main game is the castle and sending hunters after beasts, and thats where the mood and the premise actually live. If you ever feel like giving it another minute, that’s the link to try. Either way, thanks, the comparison you made is a big compliment for the mood.

comments.author: IriFlina
comments.body: i saw step 1 out of 23 in the tutorial and my eyes glazed over and i gave up after like 3 steps.

replies.author: Curious_Ad5417
replies.body: Ha, thats fair, “1 out of 23” does sound like homework. Nobody needs to see the whole list on step one, so that number is going. Thanks!

comments.author: Brief_Shopping2222
comments.body: I am immediately presented with 20 buttons and have no clue as to what to do with any of them. There are millions of games out there and I have no reason to play detective trying to figure out how a bland derivative made with Ai works. I'm not trying to be rude, but this is the reality.

replies.author: Curious_Ad5417
replies.body: Not rude at all, thats exactly the kind of thing I needed to hear. Twenty buttons before you know what the game even is, that’s a fair hit. I’m cutting the start down so you only see what you need for the next step, and the rest shows up when it actually matters.

replies.author: Brief_Shopping2222
replies.body: Glad you understand. I went through the same thing myself building a complex trading card/tactics game. I was so stoked on all my great ideas, then I went to try and play it and even I was confused lol. So simple is good at first. Players generally hate tutorials so small, intuitive options that will break them into the game are the way to go.

replies.author: Curious_Ad5417
replies.body: Ha, the trading card thing hits close to home. I actually have a small card game inside the game too and had to stop myself from adding every rule I came up with. Simple first, then let people discover the rest. Thanks for the push!

comments.author: CutMysterious9844
comments.body: Give the cards nice rarity borders or something

replies.author: Curious_Ad5417
replies.body: They actually have them, but the starter deck is almost all common cards, so you never got to see the fancy ones. The rare frames only show up once youve hunted for better cards. Probably worth giving new players one rare card early so they know what they’re hunting for. Thanks!

comments.author: Kindly-Sail6260
comments.body:
Had to sign up and immediately left. Might not be a blocker for some, but if I have to sign up to play a free browser game, it ain’t worth my time. 

But if others are saying it looks generic then you should go back to the drawing board and find out what actually makes your game fun. It don’t gotta be unique, but you have to ask yourself what makes the game fun after building a prototype. If you cant find it, iterate until it is fun. Besides, most games aren’t fun until you add that extra juice to it

replies.author: Curious_Ad5417
replies.body: That ones on me. You actually don’t need an account, theres a “play without signing in” option, but if the screen makes it look like you do, that’s just as bad. That step is going away so you can just play. And fair point on the juice, that’s the part Im digging into now.

comments.author: kosimus
comments.body:
A bit too overloaded with text right from the start. You see a bunch of things you can't interact with, and so you get overwhelmed. So that's one thing. 
But that's actually just a side note. 
More importantly: a sample of under a few hundred users is just not statistically relevant and you won't get useful info out of it. But when you do get enough people to reach some kind of meaningful conclusion, keep in mind that the retention of 20% on day 3 would make a potential business case, and bring under that number is completely normal. The vast majority of newly created online games never become financial stable to even support their own cost, not to mention turning any profit.
It's ok, and that's just how it is, is what I'm trying to say :).

replies.author: Curious_Ad5417
replies.body: Thanks, thats a really helpful perspective. You’re right about the sample size, a few dozen players tell me where it hurts but not much more, so Im treating the numbers as hints, not proof. The 20% day 3 retention mark is a great reference point, I keep an eye on that once the start is fixed. And yes, I know most games never pay for themselves. I’m building this one because it’s the game I want to play, anything beyond that is a bonus.

replies.author: kosimus
replies.body: Good luck, mate! The German (and broadly European) gaming industry has seen some success in recent decades. Who knows, maybe you'll be another success story at some point.

replies.author: Curious_Ad5417
replies.body: Thanks a lot, thats really kind! Greetings from Germany then 😄 I’ll take it one fixed first minute at a time.

comments.author: VintageOwlLabs
comments.body:
The image AI art looks mostly consistent, kudos on that.



Played for about 10mins, built, fought, then was slain.



“I describe what I want, read what comes back, playtest, complain, repeat.”

What is your actual vision for the game?

As others have mentioned it lacks any of the modern FTP manipulation/engagement techniques, relaying on those pioneered over a decade ago.



“So almost a third of my players decided the best part of a building game is not building. Fair, but I’d love to know why. “

Simple, I do not understand why I would care when the number goes up, so waiting on progress bars (a central large part of the game) is a boring experience. Other people may already start out with that opinion and not even being playing.

replies.author: Curious_Ad5417
replies.body: Thanks, glad the art holds together, that took more work than people think. The vision, I’ve been playing games for about 30 years, and this is the game I always wanted to play. A dark castle you rebuild over weeks, hunters who grow with you, a story that unfolds chapter by chapter, and a guild to share it with. Its for people who rather play one game for a long time than ten for a week. You’re right that it skips most of the modern engagement tricks. Partly that’s on purpose, I’d rather people stay because they care than because something nags them. But “why should I care when the number goes up” is the real question, and right now the first minutes don’t answer it. That’s exactly what I’m working on.

comments.author: iAteMyBunny
comments.body: I dont like games like this at all, clicking buttons and waiting. There is no gameplay

replies.author: Curious_Ad5417
replies.body: Fair enough, it’s definitely not for everyone. It meant as a phone game you check a few times a day rather than something you sit down and play for an hour. Thanks for giving it a look anyway!

comments.author: Life-Departure4088
comments.body: There is nothing to keep me engaged. At first i was a little overwhelmed. So much stuff on the screen. Then i upgraded, saw i had a bunch of resources. Found the hunt button. Clicked on the thing to hunt. It says it will take 3 minutes. Thats where i gave up. Im not waiting for 3 minutes for nothing.

replies.author: Curious_Ad5417
replies.body: Fair point, and thanks for actually trying it. The first hunt really shouldn’t make you stare at a timer before you know why you’re waiting. I’m making the very first hunt short so you see the fight right away, and pointing you to something to build in the meantime. Later the timers are part of the game, but not in minute one.

replies.author: Life-Departure4088
replies.body: Right I didnt get that experience. I actually saw the hunt maybe i would have watched. I literally thought i was sitting there for minutee just twiddling my thumbs.
